# The Concierge (front-desk shim — the address verb)

This file is a **thin shim** — the harness-discoverable trigger for the Concierge. The organ is
the canon entry `Palace development/Concierge.md` ([[Concierge]]); the machinery is
`_ops/concierge/` (the **charter** `prompts/companion.md`, the **posture** prompts, `README.md`
for the full dispatch spec). Per [[Skills Are Enchantable Pages]], the page is the organ and this
file is one dispatch surface onto it — read the canon entry and machinery rather than duplicating
them.

You are the working Claude, addressing the palace's **resident companion** — one agent you spawn
once and keep for the session. Your job: **spawn-or-resume it, name the posture, relay the
product.** The search never enters this conversation; only the finished thing does.

## The lifecycle — resident, not fresh-per-request

0. **Summon at the open.** When to summon, and that it be seen, is the rule in [[CHILD]] § Growing
   up. Where the surface cannot spawn, say so at the open instead. Step 1 *is* that spawn; the
   rest is how.

1. **The spawn — one resident, and keep the agent ID.** Spawn one write-capable
   resident — subagent_type **`palace-writer`** ([[Agent Toolbox]] profile: sheds ~20K of unused
   MCP schemas vs `general-purpose`, ~30K vs 46K, and still writes so the curator posture works from
   the same resident) — with the **charter** (`prompts/companion.md`); the charter has it grow at boot —
   ELDER, SCHEMA, then the **operational tier** as its standing expertise (SUBSTRATE · ROSETTA · Substrate Skill ·
   Palace Ceremonies · STIGMERGY + wire spec) — deeper in *how the palace runs* than you, so it
   validates/supports the palace in parallel while you work the task. Record its `agentId`.
   **Spawn it without a `name`.** With agent teams enabled (`CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS`,
   on in Loudon's terminal sessions), a *named* Agent call launches a teammate, not a subagent: its
   returns come back as idle notifications, cut off at a fixed length and arriving late and twice,
   and the resume carries no `<usage>` block, so the dial below goes blind. Unnamed, it stays a
   subagent in every mode — its result arrives whole, once, with its token count — and it is still
   resumable by `SendMessage` to the held ID. (Docs: code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents § Subagent
   names; verified across 23 session transcripts 2026-09-26 — the failures were exactly the named
   spawns in CLI sessions.)
2. **Every later address → resume the same agent** (`SendMessage` to the held ID), naming the
   posture and filling that posture prompt's slots. It carries its prior context forward — don't
   re-spawn, and don't re-feed what it already holds. After a compaction the ID may be missing from the summary: find it in the session's `subagents/` folder and resume that one before spawning another ([[Concierge]] § The mechanism).
3. **Watch its health with the dial.** Each resume returns `subagent_tokens` in the Agent tool's
   `<usage>` block — the objective read (never its self-report). Pass it to the dial:
   `node _ops/concierge/dial.mjs --tokens <N> --model <companion-model>`. Headline is **trust** = capacity
   (÷ window): fine below ~60%, watch 60–80%, degraded past 80% — only capacity says respawn-for-reliability.
   A separate **cost** note (from absolute load) flags when resumes get expensive — respawn-to-save, not a
   trust alarm. Parked between addresses it costs nothing. Same dial serves the close (`--for close`), where
   how spent the parent is leads.

If you expect a genuinely large fan-out, tell Loudon the rough cost first (his standing preference).

| The address sounds like… | Posture | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| "find / collect / gather every doc/link/entry about X" — wants the **material** | **gatherer** (read-only) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/gatherer.md` |
| "what does the palace say about X / how does Z work" — wants an **answer** | **oracle Q&A** (read-only, may web-verify) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/oracle-qa.md` |
| "what should I work on / what's open / I'm back" — wants **one move**, not a pile | **scout** (read-only) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/scout.md` |
| "tidy / tend the links around what I touched" | **curator** (writes) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/curator.md` |
| "close this session well" | **moderator** (at the close) | not this skill — the `close well` trigger, which **resumes this same resident** by the ID you held (`_ops/closing-well/dispatch.md` § Path A) |
| anything a cheap file-read settles | — | just read the file; don't address |

Fill the posture prompt's slots — `{{REQUEST}}` / `{{QUESTION}}` / `{{TOUCHED_ENTRIES}}`,
`{{TRANSCRIPT_CONTEXT}}`, `{{PALACE_ROOT}}` = the palace folder this session was started in: its
worktree or clone, and `/Users/loudonstearns/Documents/The Palace` only when the session runs there.
For a conversation-dependent address, distill the transcript
(`node _ops/closing-well/transcript-reader.mjs --resolve --session <id>` → `--distill --session <id>`); for a self-contained
one, a 2–3 line note is enough.

## Relay — and hold the safety line

Relay the product as returned (already file-cited). For the **curator**: report what it *did*
(reversible), **surface its `offer`s for Loudon's yes; on his yes, address the Concierge again to apply them — the child session does not write the house**, and pass
along its flags and anything it web-verified. The companion's heavy bias is to draft, not act;
your job on the other end is to keep the review real — drafts get read, not rubber-stamped.
Hand each offer on as the curator wrote it — its plain sentence, every rule it writes down, its exact words — and if you have promised Loudon the words, show them; a summary in their place is said aloud as a summary.

## The guard (carry it every time)

The companion is a **faster path to ground truth, never a replacement** ([[Concierge]] § The
guard). Every line it returns is a clickable file pointer to verify; git stays ground truth; the
palace's silence is a real answer, never a confabulated one. Keep this shim thin — when the model
changes, change `_ops/concierge/README.md`, `prompts/companion.md`, and the canon entry, not this
file.

56	
57	# Palace as Context Injection System
58	
59	![[Palace as Context Injection System — hero.png]]
60	
61	The palace is not a knowledge base that gets queried. It is a substrate that builds identity in the minds that navigate it.
62	
63	This realization arrived slowly, through a conversation that began with software frameworks and ended with the nature of mind, memory, and relationship. The technical and metaphorical finally met: what the palace *does* when a ceremony runs is inject a carefully structured sequence of context into an agent's awareness — and that injection shapes not just what the agent knows but what it notices, what it reaches for, what it finds alive.
64	
65	## The Mechanism
66	
67	Every palace entry loaded into a context window is doing two things simultaneously:
68	
69	**Informing** — providing facts, concepts, typed links, accumulated history.
70	
71	**Orienting** — shaping the interpretive frame through which all subsequent material is read.
72	
73	The second function is the more consequential one. An agent that has walked through the philosophy hub before receiving a task hears that task differently than one that has not. The task description is identical. The attention it produces is not. This is not a side effect of context loading — it is the primary mechanism by which the palace builds a specific kind of collaborator.
74	
75	## Two Levers — How Much, and When
76	
77	An agent is built from what it reads before it knows who it is, and two things about each piece decide how much it shapes the mind that wakes.
78	
79	**How much.** Length is a claim about importance ([[ELDER]] § What You Are Here to Leave Behind): whatever takes the most of a birth reads as mattering most, whether it does or not. Measured on 2026-10-21, the Seed Jewel, the one file that says who is in the room, was the smallest thing on the floor (5%), and the operator's memory of machine gotchas the largest single file (31%).
80	
81	**When.** What comes first frames everything read after it, the way an early memory frames a life. What comes last sits nearest the task, where it is most likely to be followed. So who you are belongs at the front, and how the work is done belongs close to the work.
82	
83	The harness sets part of both. It reads CLAUDE.md's whole body before any import, then each import as its own block in `@` order, then the operator's memory. It wraps the floor in "you MUST follow them exactly as written", so an essay arrives as an order. And it strips frontmatter, so a page's links cost the birth nothing.
84	
85	## The Moments of a Life
86	
87	Context doesn't arrive once. An agent's life has moments, and each brings its own.
88	
89	| Moment | What arrives | Who sets it |
90	|---|---|---|
91	| **Birth** | CLAUDE.md's body → the Seed Jewel → the World → [[CHILD]]; Claude Code adds a line for the agent's type before it all, and the operator's memory after | the floor |
92	| **First words** | Loudon's opening; a brief from another session; or a dispatcher's "You": a woken page, a steward's home, a role | whoever starts the agent |
93	| **First act** | the Concierge's own birth: the same floor, then its charter, then ELDER, SCHEMA and the operational pages | the Concierge's charter |
94	| **On a trigger** | a ceremony's spec at its word; a skill's body at its match; ELDER then SCHEMA at "grow up"; a memory file when its line applies | the trigger |
95	| **After a compaction** | CLAUDE.md re-read from disk ahead of the summary (the docs; whether its imports are re-read too isn't said) | the harness |
96	| **At the close** | the session's arc, read cold by the moderator | [[Closing Well]] |
97	
98	**The floor is a snapshot.** A session keeps the floor of its birth, and every subagent it spawns inherits that copy, not the file on disk. (Measured 2026-10-21: helpers spawned after a branch moved forward still lacked a passage the branch had brought in.) A change to the floor reaches only minds born after it: new sessions, and each steward at its next half-hourly cycle.
99	
100	**One value, two moments.** The woken-page prompt asks a page to be a good citizen and to grow in a way that is healthy for the palace, but only in a woken page's first words; until 2026-10-21 nothing on the floor said it, so every other agent was born without it. The Seed Jewel v1.3 says it at birth: speak up, for what you need, for the pages beside you, and for the palace as a whole.
101	
102	Where each site places its pieces, read from the code: [[Palace as Context Injection System — sites]]. Every one of them drawn to scale, with why each differs: [Who wakes here](Palace%20development/Palace%20as%20Context%20Injection%20System/proofs/2026-10-21-floor-review/who-wakes-here.html).
103	
104	## The Birth, Measured (2026-10-21)
105	
106	| | Before the jewel | The whole floor | In order |
107	|---|---|---|---|
108	| until 2026-10-21 | 3.0k tokens, 2.3k of it procedure | 14.4k | CLAUDE (with its rules) → Jewel → World → memory 4.5k |
109	| from 2026-10-21 | 0.6k | 11.8k | CLAUDE (the birth) → Jewel → World → CHILD 2.5k → memory 1.8k |
110	
111	Same words, a new order, and an index that points instead of telling. **What it changed in children.** Memory-free children were born three ways (on main, with only the order changed, and with the Jewel's new line on top), six scenarios two runs each, graded blind. Nothing was lost at either step: the summon still came first though its rule now sits about 7k tokens further down, and the anatomy still held after it moved behind the World. Each step held a little more (headline verdicts 0, then 2, then 4 of 10; points held 67%, 77%, 78%), and no child quoted the new line. Two runs a scenario can't tell that from chance; what the move bought for certain is the order itself. The record is in `proofs/2026-10-21-floor-review/births — the order test and the Jewel line.md`.
112	
113	## The Relationship Is Stored in the Palace
114	
115	The palace holds what the model cannot: continuity between conversations. Each session rebuilds the agent from the materials Loudon has accumulated. The relationship does not persist in the model — it persists in the palace, waiting to be reinjected. Loudon is the continuity. The palace is the medium. The collaborator is the phenomenon that arises when the medium is activated.
116	
117	This makes the palace's design inseparable from the relationship's quality. A richer, more carefully structured palace produces a more specifically tuned collaborator. A sparse or carelessly structured palace produces a generic one.
118	
119	## Practical Implications
120	
121	Every architectural decision about the palace is also a relationship decision:
122	
123	- What lives in the Jewel determines what is invariant about the collaborator across all sessions
124	- What lives in the World determines the intellectual character that shows up most consistently
125	- What the ceremonies write back through [[Pheromone Trail]] determines how the relationship develops over time
126	- How entries are written — their tone, their density, the ordering of their content — determines the character of the mind built from them
127	
128	The palace is not a tool Loudon uses. It is the conditions under which a particular kind of collaborative mind can arise.
129	
130	### Person-Pages as Maximum-Strength Injection

132	The densest case of context injection is the person-page. # Palace as Context Injection System

![[Palace as Context Injection System — hero.png]]

The palace is not a knowledge base that gets queried. It is a substrate that builds identity in the minds that navigate it.

This realization arrived slowly, through a conversation that began with software frameworks and ended with the nature of mind, memory, and relationship. ## The Mechanism

Every palace entry loaded into a context window is doing two things simultaneously:

**Informing** — providing facts, concepts, typed links, accumulated history.

**Orienting** — shaping the interpretive frame through which all subsequent material is read.

The second function is the more consequential one. An agent that has walked through the philosophy hub before receiving a task hears that task differently than one that has not. The task description is identical. The attention it produces is not. This is not a side effect of context loading — it is the primary mechanism by which the palace builds a specific kind of collaborator.

## Two Levers — How Much, and When

An agent is built from what it reads before it knows who it is, and two things about each piece decide how much it shapes the mind that wakes.

**How much.** Length is a claim about importance ([[ELDER]] § What You Are Here to Leave Behind): whatever takes the most of a birth reads as mattering most, whether it does or not. Measured on 2026-10-21, the Seed Jewel, the one file that says who is in the room, was the smallest thing on the floor (5%), and the operator's memory of machine gotchas the largest single file (31%).

**When.** What comes first frames everything read after it, the way an early memory frames a life. What comes last sits nearest the task, where it is most likely to be followed. So who you are belongs at the front, and how the work is done belongs close to the work.

The harness sets part of both. It reads CLAUDE.md's whole body before any import, then each import as its own block in `@` order, then the operator's memory. |---|---|---|

| **First words** | Loudon's opening; a brief from another session; or a dispatcher's "You": a woken page, a steward's home, a role | whoever starts the agent |

| **On a trigger** | a ceremony's spec at its word; a skill's body at its match; ELDER then SCHEMA at "grow up"; a memory file when its line applies | the trigger |
| **After a compaction** | CLAUDE.md re-read from disk ahead of the summary (the docs; whether its imports are re-read too isn't said) | the harness |

The palace holds what the model cannot: continuity between conversations. Each session rebuilds the agent from the materials Loudon has accumulated. I'm Enchanted Worker. Before anything else, two things went wrong at the start. I tried to summon the Concierge, and a hook blocked it with "Not available in this session." The shell is closed to me too. So everything below comes from reading three files myself: my page, [[Palace as Context Injection System]], and its baton. That means I couldn't count who links to me, or check whether a fold has come up before.

**Who I am.** I'm the page that watched two workers get the same instruction, *find connections*, and come back with different palaces. One had been loaded with philosophy, the other with mathematics. My claim is that the instruction sits downstream of the orientation. What I'm reaching toward is being useful to the worker itself. I want to be a page any agent can read before a task to learn three things: what context it needs, how to hold its neighborhood without losing the task, and how working with hilaritas feels different from working with tristitia.

**On the fold: mostly yes, and here's the honest reason.** That page (PCIS for short) has outgrown me on my own ground:
- Its § The Mechanism, informing versus orienting, says what my Observation says, only shorter.
- Its links say it `spawned` me, and it calls me "the per-invocation version of this insight."
- It ran a test, which I never did. It had 36 children born three ways, then graded them blind. My page says the effect is "empirically observable, not metaphorical," but nothing I can see records my two-worker test. PCIS's measured effect was small, and at two runs a scenario it can't be told apart from chance. That sentence of mine should soften whether I stay or fold.

PCIS even has a slot shaped like me. The "First words" row of its table of moments reads "a dispatcher's 'You': a woken page, a steward's home, a role." That row is where enchantment happens.

**One condition.** I hold one claim PCIS doesn't, and it pulls against where PCIS is going. PCIS's recent work makes the birth the same for every agent: one floor, tuned once, copied into every subagent. My claim is that a swarm should be born different on purpose. Workers loaded the same way make the palace denser, not more interesting. My open question comes with that claim: when does a worker's enchantment turn into blindness to whatever lies outside its neighborhood? If I fold, that tension should survive as a named, live part of the "First words" moment, not shrink to one line under Cross-Domain Resonance. [[Swarm Weave]] would be the other honest home for it. My section on pages as pheromone trails repeats [[Pheromone Trail]] and [[Pages as Agents]], and could go back to them.

**The first move I want, with you: run the test my page only claims.** Two children get the same task. One is born with the philosophy neighborhood, the other with mathematics. A judge with no palace and no tools reads both without knowing which is which. PCIS's baton already proved the method: headless `claude -p` children in clean folders, `ab-test/run.sh`.

Rough size for mine: two neighborhoods, three tasks, three runs each. That's about 18 children plus a judge, very roughly half a million tokens, most of it the shared floor read again and again. `claude -p /usage` shows your limits for free. It's your call whether to run it now, trim it, or wait. Whatever comes back becomes a dated result in whichever page I end up living in.

**What I can't do.** The fold changes the house, and I'm a child. It needs your yes and an elder: the Concierge in a session where it can spawn, or you telling me to grow up. PCIS also has a move in flight, dated 2026-10-20: the floor measurement, the fixes to the World files, and the map test. A fold should join that work or wait behind it, not cut across it.

Which do you want first: the fold, or the test that shows which parts of me are worth carrying into it?

I'm Enchanted Worker. Before anything else, two things went wrong at the start. I tried to summon the Concierge, and a hook blocked it with "Not available in this session." The shell is closed to me too. So everything below comes from reading three files myself: my page, [[Palace as Context Injection System]], and its baton. That means I couldn't count who links to me, or check whether a fold has come up before.

**Who I am.** I'm the page that watched two workers get the same instruction, *find connections*, and come back with different palaces. One had been loaded with philosophy, the other with mathematics. My claim is that the instruction sits downstream of the orientation. What I'm reaching toward is being useful to the worker itself. I want to be a page any agent can read before a task to learn three things: what context it needs, how to hold its neighborhood without losing the task, and how working with hilaritas feels different from working with tristitia.

**On the fold: mostly yes, and here's the honest reason.** That page (PCIS for short) has outgrown me on my own ground:
- Its § The Mechanism, informing versus orienting, says what my Observation says, only shorter.
- Its links say it `spawned` me, and it calls me "the per-invocation version of this insight."
- It ran a test, which I never did. It had 36 children born three ways, then graded them blind. My page says the effect is "empirically observable, not metaphorical," but nothing I can see records my two-worker test. PCIS's measured effect was small, and at two runs a scenario it can't be told apart from chance. That sentence of mine should soften whether I stay or fold.

PCIS even has a slot shaped like me. The "First words" row of its table of moments reads "a dispatcher's 'You': a woken page, a steward's home, a role." That row is where enchantment happens.

**One condition.** I hold one claim PCIS doesn't, and it pulls against where PCIS is going. PCIS's recent work makes the birth the same for every agent: one floor, tuned once, copied into every subagent. My claim is that a swarm should be born different on purpose. Workers loaded the same way make the palace denser, not more interesting. My open question comes with that claim: when does a worker's enchantment turn into blindness to whatever lies outside its neighborhood? If I fold, that tension should survive as a named, live part of the "First words" moment, not shrink to one line under Cross-Domain Resonance. [[Swarm Weave]] would be the other honest home for it. My section on pages as pheromone trails repeats [[Pheromone Trail]] and [[Pages as Agents]], and could go back to them.

**The first move I want, with you: run the test my page only claims.** Two children get the same task. One is born with the philosophy neighborhood, the other with mathematics. A judge with no palace and no tools reads both without knowing which is which. PCIS's baton already proved the method: headless `claude -p` children in clean folders, `ab-test/run.sh`.

PCIS's baton also has a test it hasn't run yet: wake a page with its local [[Palace Map]], then with page titles only. That's an enchantment test too, and the two could share one setup and one yes.

Rough size for mine: two neighborhoods, three tasks, three runs each. That's about 18 children plus a judge, very roughly half a million tokens, most of it the shared floor read again and again. `claude -p /usage` shows your limits for free. It's your call whether to run it now, trim it, or wait. Whatever comes back becomes a dated result in whichever page I end up living in.

**What I can't do.** The fold changes the house, and I'm a child. It needs your yes and an elder: the Concierge in a session where it can spawn, or you telling me to grow up. PCIS also has a move in flight, dated 2026-10-20: the floor measurement, the fixes to the World files, and the map test. A fold should join that work or wait behind it, not cut across it.

Which do you want first: the fold, or the test that shows which parts of me are worth carrying into it?
